name: Falangism
summary: Falangism is the doctrine of José Antonio Primo de Rivera's Falange Española (1933), joined with Ledesma's JONS. It demands a national revolution that replaces parties and parliament with a totalitarian state serving Spain's unity and imperial destiny, organises employers and workers in vertical state syndicates, rejects both capitalism and Marxism, nationalises credit and redistributes land, and keeps Catholic identity while placing the State above the Church.
scope: The founding Falange as defined in its Twenty-Six Point programme (the 1937 revised text) and José Antonio's writings, read through Payne's scholarship. Franco's FET y de las JONS regime used it as one component among Carlists, Church and army, so that regime's record is not counted; neither are later splinter parties, whose positions count only where the defining texts confirm them. Fascism, national syndicalism and Francoism are separate entries. José Antonio's founding speech of 29 October 1933 could not be opened in full, so no answer rests on it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Point 1 makes individual, group and class interests give way to the nation, and point 7 says no one may use his freedom against it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Payne reports the programme as a party-led nationalist dictatorship with all parties abolished (point 6 abolishes the party system).

total-state.rationale: Point 6 calls the state a totalitarian instrument, with education (point 23) and the economy (point 9) organised by it.

organic-representation.rationale: Point 6 has Spaniards take part through family, municipal and syndical roles and abolishes parties and 'inorganic suffrage'.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Point 9 organises society corporatively in vertical syndicates of producers and point 11 merges all who produce into one body; wage and price setting is not spelled out.

class-collaboration.rationale: Point 11 says the regime will remove the roots of class struggle because all who produce form one organic entity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Point 10 repudiates the capitalist system and, in the same point, Marxism.

public-ownership.rationale: Point 14 supports nationalising banking and, through a system of Corporations, the great public utilities.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Point 13 recognises property as a means to individual, family and social goals, and point 8 permits private initiative only if compatible with the collective interest.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is called a legitimate means rather than an overriding right (point 13), and points 19 and 21 allow redistribution and expropriation without indemnity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Point 19 redistributes arable land to revive family farms and point 18 aims to eliminate wasted latifundia; point 21 expropriates without indemnity only illegally held land.

collective-farming.rationale: Point 19 aims to revive family farms, with farm labourers syndicalised, rather than collective farming.

farm-price-support.rationale: Point 18 assures all agricultural producers a minimum remuneration, cheap national credit against usury and tariff protection for farming.

nation-first.rationale: Points 1 and 3 subordinate all interests to Spain's grandeur and reject both international isolation and foreign interference; Payne notes hostility to the Western democracies in 1937-42.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Point 3 demands an Empire and pre-eminence in Europe; Payne says its meaning was unclear, from cultural leadership to annexing Portugal.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Point 3 makes Spain the spiritual axis of Hispanic America and favours unifying its culture, economic interests and power.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Point 3 favours unifying the culture, economic interests and power of the Hispanic American countries.

civilizational-union.rationale: Point 3 favours unifying the culture, economic interests and power of the Hispanic world under Spain's lead.

military-superiority.rationale: Point 4 wants forces large and trained enough to secure Spain's independence and a status that befits it, and point 3 claims pre-eminence in Europe.

empower-police-military.rationale: Point 4 promises the armed forces all dignity and wants their military view of life to infuse Spanish life.

conscription.rationale: Point 20 mobilises all youth compulsorily for a time and point 23 gives all men paramilitary training for the National and Popular Army.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Points 20 and 23 mobilise youth and train all men paramilitarily; uniforms are not mentioned.

political-violence-never.rationale: Payne lists violence among the Falange's means of regenerating Spain, and point 26 calls its method direct, bold and combative.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Point 26 and Payne's account make combative violence a method of national revolution.

revolution-justified.rationale: Point 26 calls for a revolution to impose the new order against resistance.

direct-action.rationale: Point 26 prescribes a direct, combative method and point 6 rejects parliament and party politics.

national-rebirth.rationale: Point 26 demands a revolution for a new order and point 1 calls for strengthening and raising Spain.

gradual-change.rationale: Point 26 demands revolution against the present order rather than gradual change.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Point 6 implacably abolishes the party system and point 7 provides rigorous discipline against anything dividing Spaniards; Payne reports parties abolished.

democracy-best.rationale: Payne records that the Falange rejected liberalism and parliamentary government, and point 6 abolishes parties and parliament.

proportional-representation.rationale: Point 6 abolishes the party system and its 'inorganic suffrage'.

direct-votes.rationale: Point 6 rejects inorganic suffrage and individual political participation in favour of family, municipal and syndical roles.

right-to-secede.rationale: Point 2 calls any separatism a crime that will not be pardoned.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Point 2 treats separatism as an unpardonable crime and Payne records the aim of ending regional separatism; force is not named.

decide-locally.rationale: Point 2 and Payne stress Spain's political unity; municipalities appear only as one organ of national participation (point 6).

separate-church-state.rationale: Point 25 has the Movement incorporate the Catholic meaning of Spain's tradition and has Church and State coordinate powers; Payne says Catholicism was to be official.

more-religion-public.rationale: Point 25 and Payne make Catholic identity part of the national project.

national-church-status.rationale: Payne reports Catholicism as the official religion in Falangism and point 25 incorporates the Catholic meaning.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Point 25 refuses any Church activity impairing the State's dignity and Payne reports clerical influence in government rejected, while Catholic identity is affirmed.

religious-nation.rationale: Point 25 and Payne give the nation a Catholic identity, but the nation is defined by Spain's destiny (points 1-2).

clerical-rule.rationale: Payne reports that clerical influence in government was rejected, and point 25 keeps the State's dignity above the Church.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Point 25 gives the Movement a Catholic meaning, which an atheist state education would contradict.

religion-illusion.rationale: Point 10 founds its rejection of Marxism on a spiritual conception of life, and point 25 embraces Catholicism.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Point 10 states a spiritual and national conception of life and point 7 calls human dignity eternal.

sacred-nation.rationale: Point 1 calls Spain a supreme reality to which every interest yields, and point 26 asks for sacrifice.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Point 25 incorporates glorious tradition and point 23 teaches pride in the fatherland.

patriotic-education.rationale: Point 23 makes it the State's essential mission to instil national spirit and pride in the fatherland through disciplined education.

traditional-family.rationale: Point 6 makes the family one of the three channels of participation and point 19 revives family farms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Point 15 keeps and strengthens existing social legislation and has public agencies support those in desperate straits.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Point 16 gives all but the disabled a duty to work and withholds consideration from those who live as drones.

job-guarantee.rationale: Point 15 declares a right to work for all Spaniards, with public support for the desperate; employer of last resort is not stated.

basic-income.rationale: Point 16 imposes a duty to work and denies consideration to those who do not, which conflicts with an unconditional income.

independent-unions.rationale: Point 9 puts vertical syndicates inside the corporative organisation of the state; Payne records they were run from above under Franco.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Point 11 will prevent selfish interests abusing others and point 13 protects property from large finance capital.

public-money-creation.rationale: Point 14 supports nationalising banking and Payne describes nationalisation of credit to end usury.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Point 16 gives no consideration to those who live off the labour of others without a useful function.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Point 12 says wealth's first duty is to better the people's condition.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Point 12 states that the first duty of wealth is to better the condition of the people.

harm-principle.rationale: Point 7 allows no use of freedom against the nation and imposes rigorous discipline, which goes beyond preventing harm to others.

person-over-state.rationale: Point 1 makes individual interests yield to Spain, though point 7 calls human dignity eternal.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Points 1 and 26 put individual interest below service and sacrifice for the nation.

single-common-good.rationale: Points 1 and 11 make the nation one organic entity whose goal overrides group and class interests.

state-harmful.rationale: Point 6 makes the state a totalitarian instrument; the doctrine is the opposite of anti-statism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Points 6, 9, 14 and 23 give the state economic, educational and social tasks.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Point 6 makes the state the instrument defending the fatherland and point 4 gives defence to the state's armed forces.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Point 4 requires large trained armed forces.

arms-reduction.rationale: Point 4 wants the forces kept sufficiently large to assure independence and status.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Point 4 wants a military conception of life to infuse Spanish life and point 26 calls life a militia.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Point 1 makes class interests yield to the nation, and point 10 brings workers into the national state.

workers-nation.rationale: Point 10 brings the working classes into the national state and rejects Marxism's international class politics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Points 10, 12 and 15 join national tasks with the workers' welfare.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Point 3 tolerates no foreign interference and point 4 demands complete independence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Points 3 and 4 demand complete independence and no foreign interference.

defeat-communism.rationale: Point 10 repudiates Marxism and sets out to win its working-class followers over to the national state.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Point 11 abolishes class struggle by an organic national unity rather than by one class holding power over another.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Point 10 rejects Marxism in the name of a spiritual and national conception of life.

workers-own-party.rationale: Point 6 abolishes all parties, and point 10 aims to bring workers into the national state.

minority-veto.rationale: Point 7 demands rigorous discipline and no freedom against the nation, which rules out a dissenting minority's veto.

missingStatements.rationale: Point 16 of the programme makes work a duty for everyone not disabled and denies consideration to drones.

notes: Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, means, culture. The programme is short (26 points), so most statements, especially on ecology, technology, gender, race, immigration, criminal justice and civil liberties, are null: the defining texts are silent. Payne records that the 1930s emphases changed under Franco (violence and empire dropped after 1943, 'moderated capitalism' by 1956-57); those later regime positions are a carrying regime's and are not used. The PDF is the revised 1937 text (26 points), not the 1934 27-point original. Expect the uncertainty rule to fail.
